parts: Lesson 1: What is Home Science — Summary

Home Science is the science of managing a home. It covers ourselves, our home, family members and resources, and aims at the greatest satisfaction for the family through efficient and scientific use of resources. It is the art of managing resources efficiently and the science of achieving a healthy, happy home and a successful career. Knowing the nutrients the body needs is the science; choosing dishes that have them and serving them attractively is the art.

Home Science draws content from physics, chemistry, biology, physiology and hygiene, and equally from economics, sociology, anthropology, psychology, community development, communication, media and technology, so it is an interdisciplinary field of science and arts. Its areas are communication among family members, the family, food, the house, clothes, resources, the environment and the skills for a career.

Earlier, work was divided between men and women. Today more women work outside the home, so managing a home needs the efforts of all members and gender-based roles no longer hold. Home Science is for both boys and girls: both share household tasks, manage resources and solve problems together, and both can find varied careers in it. It also helps to set up home-based enterprises such as a boutique, catering unit, creche or day care centre.

Five major areas: Food and Nutrition (food science, clinical and community nutrition, institutional food service); Resource Management (housing and equipment, interior decoration, consumer education); Fabric and Apparel Science (clothing construction, textile science, garment designing, care of clothes); Human Development (child welfare, adolescence, marriage and family guidance, care of the elderly and special children); Communication and Extension (media, programme planning and evaluation, training, management of community service organisations). These courses are offered at graduate and postgraduate level and through distance education; NIOS offers vocational courses.

Wage employment means working for another person and receiving a wage or salary; self-employment means owning, running and financing your own enterprise. A tailor with his own shop is self-employed; the same tailor in a garment factory is in wage employment. Examples: catering (staff in canteen, cook, service staff / owner of a canteen, food service from home); food preservation and bakery (production unit staff / own production unit, home-based production); interior decoration (interior designer, furniture designer, showroom staff / own shop, home-based craft centre); housekeeping and laundry (hotel and guest-house staff, facilities manager / running a guest house, paying-guest service); dress designing (production unit or export house staff, boutique staff / owner of a boutique, hobby classes); teaching (creche, play school, day care, school or college teacher / owner of a creche, tuitions at home); communication and extension (development organisation staff, counsellor, researcher / consultancy, market research, media production); resource management and consumer education (retail staff, event management firm / event manager, small savings agent).
To succeed you need thorough knowledge, practice and experience; the school course gives only basic knowledge, so specific advanced courses are needed for a job.
